newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Kingstream says steel project backed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Kingstream says steel project backed.

text.p: Kingstream Resources NL said on Wednesday the Western Australian state government has given broad support to its proposed A$1.4 billion Midwest Iron and Steel project with Taiwan's An Feng Steel Co Ltd.
However, it said the government had raised concerns about siting a steel mill at Narngulu, near Geraldton, and has recommended the project be relocated to Oakajee, about 25 km north of Geraldton.
This could allow a deep water port, reducing shipping costs, and would be acceptable if it did not increase overall costs and delay the project, Kingstream said.

"Kingstream and An Feng are reviewing in detail the potential ramifications of relocating the plant to the Oakajee site and are continuing discussions with the government in relation to this matter," it said.
Kingstream and An Feng Steel signed a heads of agreement in May to develop the project, which is expected to produce 2.4 million tonnes of steel slab a year.
The agreement provides for An Feng to contribute 70 percent of equity and Kingstream 30 percent.
An Feng will also enter into a 10-year take or pay contract to buy Kingstream's 30 percent of the finished steel project.
Kingstream said on Wednesday the government had endorsed provisions in a state agreement for long term security over the iron resource, concessions on royalties and stamp duty concessions.

The state agreement also provided for a pipeline licence to enable the joint venturers to obtain gas from the Carnarvon Basin if they were unable to negotiate a satisfactory contract with state-owned utility AlintaGas.
